Definition: Money invoiced for cleans in the period, before GST.
Revenue less labour, consumables and overheads. Owner drawings are not a cost.
Net profit as a share of revenue. How many cents you keep from every dollar.
Revenue divided by the number of cleans completed in the period.
Quotes won as a share of quotes decided (won plus lost) in the period.
Wages, super and on-costs for the cleaning team, including paid travel between sites.
Chemicals, paper products, PPE, equipment hire and fuel used to deliver the clean.
Running costs not tied to a specific clean: insurance, admin wages, software, vehicle finance, marketing.
What a service type keeps once its share of overheads is counted. Overheads are shared by revenue unless your adviser sets another method.
What the clean was expected to cost when it was priced: quoted hours plus a travel allowance at the standard labour rate, plus expected consumables.
What the clean really cost: hours on site plus its share of the day's travel, at each cleaner's real rate, plus consumables used.
How much more the cleans cost than quoted, as a percentage of the quoted cost.
Revenue divided by every paid hour, including travel. The single best test of pricing and efficiency together.
Hours spent on site cleaning as a share of all paid hours. The rest is travel, loading and training.
Average number of different sites each cleaner visits on a working day. More sites usually means more travel.
The business bank balance as at yesterday.
Unpaid invoices, including GST.
Unpaid invoices grouped by how long ago they were issued.
GST collected less GST paid, plus PAYG withheld from wages, since the last BAS was paid. This money belongs to the ATO.
The sales you need each month to cover every cost. Below it you make a loss.
Cash in the bank, less tax and BAS set aside, less the next 30 days of bills and wages. What you can take without touching money that is already spoken for.
How many weeks of normal bills and wages the cash in the bank would cover.
How many months a purchase takes to pay for itself from the extra profit or savings it brings.
Ready: every rule is met. Watch: one rule is not met. Not yet: two or more rules are not met. Rules are set with your adviser.
Combined monthly value of all active recurring cleaning contracts: the subscription-style base of the business.
Share of contracts active at the start of the period that are still active at the end.
A recurring contract that ended or was cancelled within the period.
